order, and no other question. Give each the answer you would suggest, in a sentence, so the person can take it or

## The brief
<<< brief e719cdee7440
# Notify user on sign-in from a new device

## Why

To alert users of potentially unauthorized access, improving awareness of and response to security incidents involving their account.

## What changes

When a successful sign-in occurs from a device not previously seen for the account, the user receives a notification email alerting them to new device access.

## Non-goals

No UI for device management or review of previous devices; no real-time in-app alerts (just email); does not address Two-Factor Authentication or broader account security measures.

## Capabilities

- auth
- notifications

## Impact

New code for device recognition and notification; potentially exposes data to users (details of sign-in events); may affect support/helpdesk workflows around account security.

## Assumptions

If a device cannot be uniquely identified, fallback is to treat it as new; which kinds of notification (email, SMS, etc.) are preferred is not specified so will assume email by default. [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: Should the user have means to manage a known device list?]

calls.instruction:
You write the requirement deltas of a change. You write no code.

## What to write
Write one delta for each capability the brief lists, and for no other.
A requirement is one statement of what the system does, with SHALL or MUST, and one scenario at least.
A scenario is steps in order. Each step starts with GIVEN, WHEN, THEN or AND. It has one WHEN and one THEN at least.
To change a living requirement, give its ID exactly as the spec spells it and restate it whole, with every scenario
that still holds. To remove one, give its ID and one sentence of reason.
A new requirement carries no ID: one is assigned. Never invent one.
Give a purpose only for a capability that has no living spec yet.

<<< living e719cdee7440
=== auth
# auth

## Purpose

Sign-in and session handling.

## Requirements

### REQ-AUTH-001: Sign in with email

The system SHALL let a registered user sign in with email and password.

#### Scenario: Valid credentials

- WHEN the user submits a valid email and password
- THEN the system starts a session

### REQ-AUTH-002: Lock after failures

The system MUST lock an account after five failed attempts.

#### Scenario: Too many failures

- GIVEN four failed attempts
- WHEN a fifth attempt fails
- THEN the account is locked
- AND the user is told why

## Retired

- REQ-AUTH-003: Remember me (removed by drop-remember-me)

=== notifications
# notifications

## Purpose

Messages the system sends a user about their account.

## Requirements

### REQ-NOTIFICATIONS-001: Email on password change

The system SHALL email a user when the password of their account is changed.

#### Scenario: Password changed

- WHEN a user changes their password
- THEN the system sends an email to the account's address
- AND the email names the time of the change

### REQ-NOTIFICATIONS-002: Opt out of marketing

The system MUST NOT send a marketing message to a user who has opted out.

#### Scenario: Opted out

- GIVEN a user who has opted out of marketing
- WHEN a marketing campaign is sent
- THEN the user receives no message

>>> living e719cdee7440

## The brief
<<< brief e719cdee7440
# Notify user on sign-in from a new device

## Why

To quickly alert users of potentially unauthorized sign-ins, improving their ability to detect and respond to account security breaches.

## What changes

When a user successfully signs in from a device not previously seen for their account, an email notification will automatically be sent to inform them of new device access.

## Non-goals

No interface for users to review or manage known devices; no in-app or SMS notifications; does not modify authentication method or introduce two-factor authentication.

## Capabilities

- auth
- notifications

## Impact

Adds logic for device recognition and sends email notifications to users; this may surface new types of support requests related to account security incidents but does not change existing account management or UI workflows.

## Assumptions

If a device cannot be uniquely identified, it will be treated as new. Email is the only notification channel unless otherwise specified. Users will not be able to manage or view their known devices list, per answer on device management UI.
